title: Bram and the Wreck
premise: Juniper Brightwater, a disgraced railroad engineer drowning in debt, salvages a river-wrecked chest bearing the seal of Vhalen, a nation erased from every map. Inside is a compass that points not north but toward the drowned capital's forbidden source, and a ledger of names — including his own father's. Hunted by the Consortium, the merchant power that bought Vhalen's erasure and now corrupts memory itself through licensed 'recall houses,' Juniper travels upstream with a fugitive archivist named Sable who claims to remember what everyone else was made to forget. At the source, Juniper learns his father helped erase Vhalen and paid with his own memories; choosing truth over safety, Juniper floods the Consortium's recall engine with the nation's restored past, ending its monopoly on memory at the cost of the compass, the debt, and any easy return to his old life.
about_author: Marguerite Blackwood is the pen name of a former surveyor's assistant who spent six years mapping river towns before turning to fiction. She writes adventure stories about people whose professions leave ink on their hands and maps in their dreams.

chapters.title: The River Gives Up Its Dead
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Drowning in debt to the Consortium's loan office, Juniper dredges closed rail lines for salvage and pulls up a chest stamped with Vhalen's impossible seal. Inside: a compass needle spinning toward the river's source and a ledger naming his long-dead father. The beat is wary fascination curdling into dread as he realizes the chest was meant to be found.

chapters.title: Men Who Buy Silence
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Consortium collectors arrive within hours, too fast to be coincidence, demanding the chest. Juniper flees with only the compass and ledger, learning the hard way that his employer sold his debts to men who collect more than money. The emotional beat is betrayal — the ordinary world he trusted was never neutral.

chapters.title: Sable Remembers
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Hiding in a river town's black-market archive, Juniper meets Sable, an unlicensed archivist who reads the ledger and speaks fluent Vhaleni — a language no one should know. She reveals the recall houses that rewrite citizens' memories for a fee. The beat is vertigo: history itself has been edited, and she is living proof.

chapters.title: Upstream Against the Current
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The pair boards a coal barge working the last permitted stretch of river, pursued by Consortium agent Corvane, who offers Juniper debt forgiveness for the compass. A night ambush forces them overboard. The beat is reluctant partnership hardening into trust as they choose each other over survival odds.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot Its Name
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. They shelter in Harrow's Bend, a town whose residents cannot recall anything older than twenty years — a recall-house test site. An old lockkeeper's fragmentary memories of Vhalen match entries in the ledger, including Juniper's father's signature. The beat is grief: erasure doesn't just kill nations, it hollows the people left behind.

chapters.title: What Father Signed
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Deciphering the ledger fully, Sable discovers Juniper's father was Vhalen's chief engineer who traded the nation's archive to the Consortium in exchange for his son's protected future — then had his own memory stripped as payment. She hesitates to tell him. The beat is moral weight: truth as a burden you can choose to carry or withhold.

chapters.title: Corvane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Cornered at a checkpoint, Juniper accepts Corvane's deal — safe passage in exchange for the compass — but Sable swaps it with a decoy forged from her archive work. When Corvane discovers the trick, he burns the barge and takes hostages from Harrow's Bend. The beat is guilt; cleverness has a price paid by others.

chapters.title: The Source of All Lines
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Climbing beyond the closed lines into the mountains, they find the source: not water but the Recall Engine, built atop Vhalen's flooded capital, drawing the nation's memories up like ore. Juniper confronts his father, alive, memoryless, tending the machine that ate his country. The beat is devastating recognition without reunion.

chapters.title: Everything the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax: Corvane arrives with hostages to force total erasure of the recovered archive. Sable feeds the ledger into the Engine while Juniper reverses its flow, releasing Vhalen's memories downstream to every town along the river. His father chooses to stand with them and dies holding the floodgates open. The beat is sacrifice transfiguring power into witness.

chapters.title: A Map With New Lines
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Resolution: the Consortium's monopoly collapses as riverside towns remember aloud; Vhalen reappears on maps drawn by hand, imperfectly. Debt-free but unlicensed, Juniper and Sable begin surveying honest lines for a railroad to the restored capital, his father's compass retired on a mantel. The beat is quiet hope — identity rebuilt from remembered truth.
